## Margin trends: AMD vs. NVDA

Note the fiscal calendars differ — AMD's quarters end near calendar quarter-ends; NVDA's fiscal year ends in late January, so its "2026-04-26" quarter is its most recent. Q4 figures for both (AMD 2023-12-30, 2024-12-28, 2025-12-27; NVDA 2024-01-28, 2025-01-26, 2026-01-25) are **derived** by the tool (FY minus Q1–Q3), not directly filed facts.

### Gross margin
| Period | AMD | Period | NVDA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-03-30 | 46.8% | 2024-04-28 | 78.4% |
| 2024-09-28 | 50.1% | 2024-10-27 | 74.6% |
| 2024-12-28 (derived) | 50.7% | 2025-01-26 (derived) | 73.0% |
| 2025-03-29 | 50.2% | 2025-04-27 | 60.5% |
| 2025-06-28 | 39.8% | 2025-07-27 | 72.4% |
| 2025-09-27 | 51.7% | 2025-10-26 | 73.4% |
| 2025-12-27 (derived) | 54.3% | 2026-01-25 (derived) | 75.0% |
| 2026-03-28 | 52.8% | 2026-04-26 | 74.9% |
| 2026-06-27 | 53.8% | — | — |

Both show a single sharp one-quarter trough — AMD at 39.8% (Q2 FY25, filed 2026-08-05) and NVDA at 60.5% (Q1 FY26, filed 2026-05-20) — then a full recovery. The filings themselves aren't parsed by these tools, so I can't confirm the cause from source here.

### Operating margin
- **AMD:** 0.7% (2024-03-30) → 10.6% (2024-09-28) → −1.7% (2025-06-28, an operating loss of −$134M) → 13.7% → 17.1% (derived Q4) → 14.4% → **17.3%** (2026-06-27).
- **NVDA:** 64.9% (2024-04-28) → 61.1% (derived Q4, 2025-01-26) → 49.1% (2025-04-27) → 60.8% → 63.2% → 65.0% (derived Q4) → **65.6%** (2026-04-26).

### Net margin
- **AMD:** 2.2% (2024-03-30) → 6.3% (derived Q4 2024-12-28) → 13.4% → 14.7% (derived) → 13.5% → **19.9%** (2026-06-27).
- **NVDA:** 57.1% (2024-04-28) → 56.2% (derived Q4) → 42.6% (2025-04-27) → 56.5% → 56.0% → 63.1% (derived) → **71.5%** (2026-04-26). The latest 71.5% net margin exceeds NVDA's own 65.6% operating margin that quarter, which implies a large below-the-line contribution — worth checking the filing directly.

### Revenue growth (YoY)
- AMD: 35.9% → 31.7% → 35.6% → 34.1% → 37.8% → **50.1%** (2026-06-27) — accelerating.
- NVDA: 122.4% → 93.6% → 77.9% → 69.2% → 55.6% (trough, 2025-07-27) → 62.5% → 73.2% → **85.2%** (2026-04-26) — decelerated through mid-2025, then re-accelerated.

### What the data shows on positioning
- **Absolute profitability: NVDA, decisively.** Every NVDA margin line sits far above AMD's in every comparable quarter — its worst gross margin quarter in this window (60.5%) is still above AMD's best (54.3%).
- **Direction of travel: both improving, AMD from a much lower base.** AMD's operating margin went from near-zero/negative to 17.3%, its widest in this window; NVDA's operating margin is also at its window high (65.6%). Neither is in margin compression as of the latest print.
- **Growth: AMD is accelerating off a smaller base; NVDA re-accelerated off a very large one** (85.2% YoY on $81.6B quarterly revenue vs. AMD's 50.1% on $11.5B).
- **Market pricing (Yahoo Finance, as of 2026-08-21, not SEC data):** AMD trades at trailing P/E 118.3, forward P/E 30.0, EV/EBITDA 78.7, P/S 18.3. NVDA trades at trailing P/E 33.1, forward P/E 16.7, EV/EBITDA 31.6, P/S 20.7. So the market is pricing much more future margin/earnings expansion into AMD than into NVDA on trailing earnings, despite NVDA's structurally higher margins.

The short read: NVDA is better positioned on the level and stability of margins; AMD has the steeper improvement slope but is still operating roughly a third of NVDA's margin structure, and carries the higher trailing multiple. I'm reporting what the filings and market data show, not making a recommendation.
